l: 1) Invite Realm Bot to Your Discord Server
p: Realm Bot must be present in your Discord server before you can run the connection command.
Use the /invite command or invite via: https://realmbot.dev/invite
Grant the required permissions. Administrator is recommended for full functionality.
Important: If Realm Bot cannot post messages or cannot read channels where you plan to use features (logs, chat relay, leaderboards), setup may succeed but modules will not operate correctly.

l: 2) Ensure You Have the Correct Access
p: You should be:
The Realm Owner, or a trusted administrator with access to manage the Realm
The Discord server owner or an Administrator to select the server in the dashboard. Manage Server alone is not sufficient.
Link the Microsoft/Xbox account that manages the Realms you want to connect.
Go to the dashboard: https://dashboard.realmbot.dev
Sign in with Discord.
Select Connect Microsoft Account to link your Microsoft/Xbox account.
Connect Microsoft Account
Security Note: Only link an account you trust to administrate the Realm. Treat account linking as privileged access.

Warning: Check the selected Discord server and Xbox account before connecting. If a returned Realm is already associated with another Discord server, connecting moves its association, disables its Realm Bot modules and clears their configurations. Record any settings you need to keep. This does not transfer ownership in Minecraft.
Choose one route. Both refresh the Realms associated with your linked Xbox account:

Dashboard: Select the intended server. After Connect Microsoft Account, select Connect Realms. On a server with no connected Realms, the same action is available from Server Overview > Connect Realms.

Discord: In the intended server, run /connect in a channel where Realm Bot can respond. If someone referred you, you can enter their code in the optional referral_code field. See Referrals for eligibility.
Confirm that the expected Realms appear in the server dashboard before configuring modules.
Choose your Realm (if prompted)
Review Bot Join Settings (how the relay/bot connects)
Configure Gametest Pack Management (only if required by your modules)
Enable the features you need in Realm Modules. If you use a Tebex store, follow Tebex setup.
For command help in Discord, run /help.

l: “I can’t see my Realms in the dashboard.”
p: Confirm you linked the correct Microsoft/Xbox account.
Ensure the account actually owns (or has access to) the Realms you expect.
Re-open the dashboard and refresh after linking.
Realm Bot is invited to the server and is online.
You are running /connect in a server channel where the bot has permission to respond.
Your role has sufficient permissions to run management commands (server admin recommended).

l: Xbox/Microsoft privacy blocks linking or access.
p: Check whether the linked Xbox account's privacy settings allow access to the required profile and Realm information, then retry.
Open the Realm Modules Overview to configure features.
Review Relay Account and GameTest Dependencies before enabling live or GameTest-dependent modules.
Configure Permissions and Discord channel access before giving staff operational control.
Use Troubleshooting when an automated entry check reports private title history.
Understand the Server Dashboard overview, including Premium status, linked account details, connected Realms, and where to configure server-wide settings.
Open your Discord server's Overview to check Premium status, verify the linked accounts, or select a connected Realm.
Server Dashboard Overview
Premium Status shows whether Premium is active and how much time remains.
With Premium, use Bot Server Profile to change Realm Bot's avatar and nickname for this Discord server.
See Bot Server Profile for supported images, nickname limits, and reset controls.
Choose a Discord channel to receive official Realm Bot announcements. See Updates Channel for subscribing, changing the destination or stopping delivery.
Check the Discord username and Xbox gamertag. The Xbox account identifier (XUID) may also be shown.
If a Realm is missing, check that the correct Microsoft/Xbox account is linked.
Unexpected permissions or access issues can be caused by linking a non-owner account.
Select View beside the Realm you want to manage.

A list of all connected Realms is shown at the bottom. Selecting a Realm expands its available Realm pages and configuration areas.
Confirm Premium status (if applicable)
Verify Linked User Information (correct Discord + Xbox account)
Confirm your Realms appear under Connected Realms
Configure Permissions / Allowlist before enabling staff tooling
Configure Log Channels so actions are auditable
Proceed into Realm-specific pages for modules and world configuration
Ensure the correct Microsoft/Xbox account is linked.
Re-run the linking flow in Account Linking if needed.
Confirm the account actually owns or has access to the Realms expected.
Review Permissions and Allowlist first.
Restrict high-impact areas to trusted administrator roles only.

l: “I can’t access a page from the sidebar.”
p: Confirm your role has permission for that section.
Ensure the bot has the required Discord permissions in the server.
Complete the recommended setup checklist for your Discord server, including logging, permissions, warn presets, and account linking.
Use Server Setup to configure moderation and member verification for your Discord server.
Server Setup Page
Select Configure for an incomplete step or Review to change an existing setting.
Logging: Choose staff-only channels for moderation logs and give Realm Bot permission to post there.
Permissions: Grant each Discord role only the commands it needs. Reserve management actions for trusted staff.
Warn Settings: Set warning reasons and ban thresholds to match your server rules.
Account Linking: Check the Discord and Microsoft/Xbox accounts before enabling verification or automatic invitations. Use only trusted accounts for administrative access.

This optional setting is on the server's Overview, not one of the setup checklist steps. Use it to receive Realm Bot's published patch notes, feature alerts and announcements in Discord. Premium is not required.
Grant Realm Bot Manage Webhooks in the intended Discord text or announcement channel.
Open Overview > Bot Updates & Announcements and choose Select updates channel.
Choose the channel and select Subscribe Channel. To move the subscription, use Update Channel. To stop it, use Remove > Confirm Remove.

When Realm Bot joins a server with a designated Discord Community Updates channel, it attempts to subscribe that channel if the announcement source is configured and the bot has permission. If it was not subscribed, set it up manually. Dismissing the setup prompt does not unsubscribe a channel.

If two channels receive posts after a move, the new subscription may have succeeded while removal of the old one failed. Remove the stale follower in the old channel's Settings > Integrations, or restore Manage Webhooks and retry.

l: A step shows as incomplete after configuration
p: Open the incomplete step and check its required settings.
Ensure Realm Bot has the required Discord permissions for the feature (especially for logging).

l: Review buttons work, but modules still fail
p: Server Setup covers foundational configuration. Some Realm modules additionally require:
Realm-specific configuration (inside the Realm dashboard)
A Relay Account to be in-game (for certain modules)
Gametest Pack dependencies (for advanced Realm features)
Configure which Discord channels receive Realm Bot moderation logs, including bans, unbans, kicks, and warnings.
Choose where Realm Bot posts bans, unbans, kicks and warnings in Discord.
Log Channels Configuration
Best Practice: Keep log channels staff-only and read-only for most roles. Avoid using public channels for moderation logs.
Create (or choose) one or more staff-only Discord channels, for example:
#mod-logs
#staff-commands
#audit-log
In Log Channels, select the destination channel for each log type:
Ban Logs
Unban Logs
Kick Logs
Warn Logs
Ensure Realm Bot has the required permissions in each selected channel:
View Channel
Send Messages
Read Message History (recommended)
If logs are not posting: the first thing to verify is channel permissions.

l: Option A - Single Consolidated Log Channel (Simple)
p: Route all log types to one channel, such as #mod-logs. This is appropriate for smaller teams and lower activity.

l: Option B - Split by Severity (Recommended for Staff Teams)
p: #warnings-and-kicks → Warn Logs + Kick Logs
#ban-and-unban → Ban Logs + Unban Logs
Use separate channels for each log type. This is most suitable for large servers with frequent moderation activity.
Ensure senior staff can review logs even if moderators cannot delete or edit messages.
If your server is using multiple Realms, keep your log structure consistent across them to reduce staff confusion.
Configure how members link their Minecraft account to Discord, including automatic role assignment, optional nickname syncing, auto-invites to selected Realms, and join log reporting.
Account Linking verifies that a Discord member controls the Minecraft account they link.
Account Linking Configuration
When enabled, members can link their Minecraft account to Discord using the Realm Bot linking flow.
When enabled, Realm Bot will update a user’s Discord nickname to match their Minecraft username after linking.
Before enabling, ensure:
Realm Bot has Manage Nicknames permission in your Discord server
Realm Bot’s role is above the roles of users whose nicknames it needs to edit (Discord role hierarchy)
Your server rules allow nickname automation (some communities prefer members to control nicknames themselves)
Note: If permissions or role hierarchy prevent nickname changes, linking can still succeed, but nickname syncing may fail.
Select one or more Discord roles to automatically assign when a member successfully links.
Best practice: Assign only the minimum role(s) needed for access. Keep staff roles manual.
Choose which connected Realm(s) should automatically invite users when they link their account.
Operational notes:
Auto-invite should be limited to trusted Realms (avoid auto-inviting to testing/admin Realms).
If a Realm is missing from the dropdown, confirm it is connected and visible under your linked Xbox account context.
Select a Discord channel where Realm Bot will post account linking events (e.g., successful links, key outcomes, and related system messages as supported).
Recommended setup:
Use a staff-only channel (e.g., #join-logs or #verification-logs)
Ensure Realm Bot has:
View Channel
Send Messages
Read Message History (recommended)
Enable Account Linking
Set Linked Account Roles to a standard member role (e.g., Member / Verified)
Enable Auto-invite to Realms only for your primary public/member Realm
Set a dedicated Join Logs Channel
Enable Change Nickname only if your staff team wants enforced identity consistency
Confirm the selected role exists and is still selected.
Ensure Realm Bot’s role is above the target role(s) in Discord role hierarchy.
Verify Realm Bot has Manage Roles permission.
Ensure Change Nickname is enabled.
Ensure Realm Bot has Manage Nicknames permission.
Check role hierarchy: Realm Bot must be above the member’s highest role.
Confirm the Realm is selected under Auto-invite to Realms.
Verify the Realm is connected and available under the linked Xbox account context.
If your Realm has strict membership limits, ensure you have capacity for new invites.
Configure the automated moderation messages sent to players when actions are taken, using variables to keep messages consistent, informative, and compliant.
Choose which Xbox messages Realm Bot sends to players after a kick, ban, unban or warning.
Message Actions Notice and Variables
Moderation messages are sent through your Xbox account. You are responsible for ensuring any content sent is compliant with the Xbox Community Standards and appropriate for your audience.
Practical implications:
Avoid harassment, threats, slurs, or inflammatory language
Keep messages factual, calm, and procedural
Do not share personal data or internal staff discussion
For each moderation action, you can:
Enable the message type (per action)
Customise the message text
Insert variables so the message automatically adapts to each case
Message Templates (Kick / Ban / Unban / Warn)
Insert a variable where you want its value to appear:
{user} - the staff member or account that performed the action
{target} - the player who received the action
{reason} - the reason provided (if any)
{length} - the action duration (if applicable)
{guild} - your Discord server name/identifier
{realm} - the Realm name/context
Tip: Always include {reason} where possible. A clear reason reduces disputes and repeat offences.
Message
What to include
Kick
The reason and whether the player can rejoin.
Ban
The reason, duration if temporary, and where to appeal.
Unban
Confirmation that the ban has been removed and any conditions for rejoining.
Warn
The behaviour to change and the consequence of another warning.
{target}, you were removed from {realm}. Reason: {reason}. You may rejoin if you follow the rules.
{target} was kicked from {realm} by {user}. Reason: {reason}.
{target}, you have been banned from {realm}. Reason: {reason}. Duration: {length}.
{target}, you have been banned from {realm}. Reason: {reason}. If you believe this is an error, contact staff in {guild}.
{target}, your ban has been removed in {realm}. Please review the rules before rejoining.
{target}, you have received a warning in {guild}. Reason: {reason}. Please stop this behaviour to avoid further action.
Warning issued to {target}. Reason: {reason}.
Keep messages short and factual. Players should understand the action within one read.
Avoid staff-only detail (internal notes, accusations, speculation).
Use consistent phrasing across Kick/Ban/Warn so players recognise official notices.
If you support appeals, reference a single channel or process-do not argue in-game.
Leave {reason} blank only when necessary; otherwise make it mandatory in your workflow.
Confirm the specific message type toggle is enabled (Kick/Ban/Unban/Warn).
Ensure your moderation commands include a reason and duration where applicable.
If your implementation depends on a linked Xbox account for outbound messages, verify the correct account is linked and operational.
Ensure variables match the supported format exactly: {user}, {target}, {reason}, {length}, {guild}, {realm}.
Avoid extra spaces inside braces (e.g., { reason }).
Configure warning types with custom reasons and thresholds, allowing consistent moderation and automatic escalation based on the number of warnings issued.
The Warn Settings page allows you to define structured warning types for your server. Each warning type has:
A reason (what the warning represents)
A Warnings Until Ban threshold (how many times that warning type can be issued before an automatic ban)
Warning System Configuration
Warnings are organised by type. When a staff member issues a warning of a given type (e.g., Spamming), Realm Bot records it against the user.
The configured Warnings Until Ban value determines the automatic escalation point:
If Warnings Until Ban = 3, the user will be banned after receiving three warnings of that type
If Warnings Until Ban = 1, a single warning of that type triggers an immediate ban (use sparingly)
Operational Note: Warning thresholds apply per warning type. This allows you to treat different behaviours with different severity (e.g., spamming vs cheating).
Open Create Warning Type and set the following fields.
Enter a short reason that matches a server rule.
Examples:
Spamming
Harassment
Staff Disrespect
Cheating
Inappropriate Language
Best practice: Keep reasons short, clear, and consistent with your server rules.
The number of warnings of this type required before an automatic ban is applied.
Suggested thresholds:
1 - Severe behaviours (e.g., cheating, doxxing threats, extreme harassment)
3 - Moderate behaviours (e.g., spamming, repeated minor disruption)
5 - Lower severity behaviours (e.g., minor disrespect, low-level nuisance)
When ready, select Add Warning Type to create it.
Find the warning type by its reason and threshold, then choose an action:
Edit (pencil icon) - change the reason or threshold
Delete (trash icon) - remove the warning type
Important: If you delete a warning type, update the staff guidance that refers to it.

l: Keep the List Small and Meaningful
p: Aim for warning types that map directly to your rule categories. Too many types slows staff down and makes enforcement inconsistent.
A practical baseline for most servers:
Spamming (3)
Harassment (2–3)
Staff Disrespect (5)
Cheating (1)
Inappropriate Content (1–2)
Set thresholds based on the harm level:
Immediate ban for “zero tolerance” rules
Multi-strike for behaviour that can be corrected
Tell staff:
which warning types to use for common situations
what evidence is required for severe types (e.g., cheating)
Increase Warnings Until Ban for the relevant warning type
Split overly broad warning types into “minor” vs “severe” categories (only if necessary)

l: Staff are issuing inconsistent warning reasons
p: Reduce the number of warning types
Rename warning reasons to match your rules exactly
Provide staff examples of which type to use for each scenario
Control how Realm Bot displays player information in commands, including a compact view or a more detailed output for moderation and auditing.
Choose how much player information Realm Bot shows in Discord commands such as /realm players.
Mode
Information shown when available
Compact Display
Player name and device type
Detailed Display
Player name, device type and the player's Minecraft Realm permission
Use Compact Display if staff do not need the extra profile details. Changing the display does not grant command permissions.
Control which Discord roles can use specific Realm Bot commands by assigning granular permissions per role.
Assign Realm Bot commands to Discord roles under Permissions.
Role Permissions Overview
Grant individual actions or command groups. Changes apply immediately to every member with the selected role.
Discord members with the Administrator permission bypass Realm Bot's custom role map. Other Discord permissions, such as Manage Server, do not automatically grant every Realm Bot command.
Important: Only commands that participate in Realm Bot's permission framework are governed by these role settings. Some public utility commands remain available without a custom role assignment.
Channel-based systems are separate:
Realm Console access is controlled primarily by who can send messages in its Discord channel.
Discord-to-Realm Chat Relay access is controlled primarily by who can send messages in the relay channel.
Embed Panel buttons are available to users who can view and interact with the panel.
Realm Bot role settings do not replace careful Discord channel permission configuration.
Find the role in Manage Role Permissions. Search by role name if needed.
Select the edit icon on the role card to open that role’s permission configuration.
Permissions are grouped by feature area. When editing a role, you will see categories such as:
Realm (invites, kicks/bans, realm code, open/close, slots, players, backups)
World (execute, broadcast, join/leave, live actions)
Warn (add/lookup/remove warnings)
Allowlist (add/check/list/remove allowlist entries)
Player (lookup and player-level info commands)
Verify (verification/embed or onboarding utilities)
Banlist (lookup or list ban records, where supported)
Watchlist (add, list, and remove watched players)
Each category includes a Select All option to quickly grant everything within that section—use this cautiously.
Role Permission Editor
Manage Lockdown System permits /realm lockdown and /realm unlock.
Watchlist Add, Watchlist List, and Watchlist Remove control the corresponding /watchlist actions separately.
These permissions do not exempt a staff member's Minecraft account from Lockdown. Configure the Lockdown Exempt List and Watchlist notification settings separately under Realm Security.
Grant full permissions, including:
Realm code changes
Ban/unban
World execute
Backups/world replacement tools (if present)
Permission editing itself (if available)
Grant operational moderation + management, but limit high-risk actions:
Kick/ban/unban (optional)
Player lookup, realm players, recents
Warnings and allowlist management
Limited world actions if required (broadcast/live), avoid World Execute unless fully trusted
Grant routine moderation only:
Kick (optional)
Warn add/lookup/remove
Player lookup
Allowlist check/list
View realm players
Minimal access:
Player lookup
Allowlist check/list
Verify tools (if your server uses them)
No kick/ban and no realm management
Security guideline: Treat World Execute and realm code management as high-risk. Only grant these to trusted administrators.

l: “Staff can’t use commands they should have”
p: Confirm the correct role was edited (many servers have similarly named roles).
Ensure the user actually has that role in Discord.
Check that you enabled the specific permission (e.g., Realm Kick is separate from Realm Ban).

l: “Too many people can run dangerous commands”
p: Remove Select All usage for broad categories.
Create a dedicated “Technical Admin” role for high-impact permissions.
Split moderation (Warn/Kick) from infrastructure controls (Code Change/Execute).
Keep permission sets as small as possible per role.
Review your permissions after staff changes or major server restructuring.
If you use automated onboarding roles, ensure new members do not inherit staff permissions accidentally.
Maintain an allowlist of trusted users who can bypass automated enforcement systems such as Member Gate, Bot Detection, and Skin Filtering.
Use the Allowlist to exempt specific trusted players from automated checks.
When a user is on the allowlist:
They can bypass Member Gate
They can bypass Bot Detection
They can bypass Skin Filtering
Important: The allowlist is designed for exceptions. Adding too many users reduces the effectiveness of your automated protections.
Use the Search or Add field to find a player and add them to your allowlist.
For example, add a staff or test account that needs an exception to a specific rule.
Each allowlisted entry can be removed using the delete icon on the right-hand side of the row.
Best practice: Remove access when:
a staff member steps down
a trusted account changes hands
you no longer need exceptions for a temporary tester
Periodically review the list (weekly or monthly for large servers), especially if your realm uses public codes or sees frequent traffic.

l: Prefer Fixing the Rule Before Allowlisting Everyone
p: If many legitimate players are being blocked, consider:
loosening Member Gate conditions
disabling Experimental Bot Detection
adjusting thresholds (e.g., gamerscore criteria)
using allowlist only for edge cases
No. The allowlist is intended to bypass automated gatekeeping systems such as Member Gate, Bot Detection, and Skin Filtering. It does not override manual bans or realm-level enforcement actions.
Only staff who need reliable access should be allowlisted. For larger teams, consider allowlisting senior roles only, and rely on correct Member Gate rules for everyone else.
Review and audit moderation actions taken across your connected realms, with filtering and per-user history views.
Use Moderation Logs to review bans, kicks, warnings and reversals across your connected Realms.
By default, Moderation Logs use a timeline view that groups actions by user.
Each user row shows:
gamertag / identity
a unique identifier (e.g., XUID where available)
last activity timestamp
a count indicator for logged actions
Expand a user to view their full action history, including:
action type (e.g., Ban)
date/time of the action
moderator responsible
reason text (if provided)
realm the action was applied to
Search for a player to review their previous actions and reasons.
Select a type in All Actions to show only bans, kicks, warnings or reversals.
Use Table View to compare recent actions across players rather than opening each player's timeline.
Require reasons for major actions. A consistent reason standard improves future moderation decisions and appeals.
Review logs routinely. Weekly checks help catch misuse or inconsistencies early.
Use logs for escalation. A repeat pattern visible in the timeline is often the clearest justification for longer bans or permanent removal.
Moderation Logs reflect actions issued through Realm Bot and associated systems.
If your staff use additional in-game-only moderation, those actions may not appear unless they are executed through Realm Bot workflows.
Create secure, shareable invite links (realmbot.link/...) that let players join your Minecraft Bedrock Realms through a controlled, auditable flow with optional VPN/Tor blocking.

Invite Links allow you to generate short, shareable URLs (for example, realmbot.link/my-realm) that invite players to a selected Minecraft Bedrock Realm associated with your Discord server. This system is designed to provide a safer alternative to distributing official Realm invite codes publicly, reducing repeated abuse from malicious bot accounts.
Platform Note: Invite Links are intended for Minecraft Bedrock Realms.
Realm Invites Management
Invite Links help Realm Owners:
Share a Realm invite through a controlled join flow rather than exposing a raw Realm code
Enforce basic security checks (such as VPN/Hosting/Tor blocking, where enabled)
Limit exposure using max uses and expiry dates
Disable or rotate links quickly if a link is leaked or targeted
When a user opens an Invite Link in their browser, they are brought to a dedicated invite page for the Realm.
Invite Acceptance Page
To accept the invite, the user will be asked to securely sign in with their Microsoft account. After acceptance:
the Realm invite is applied to their Microsoft account
the Realm appears in their Minecraft Realms list in-game
Server Account Linking can also support automatic invitations, but it is a separate Microsoft verification workflow rather than the same public Invite Link acceptance page.
Security Clarification: Users authenticate through Microsoft’s standard login flow. Players should only sign in on pages they trust and should verify the domain before proceeding.
When enabled, players attempting to use invite links through VPNs, hosting providers, or Tor can be blocked from completing the invite flow.
This is recommended for:
public invite advertising
Realms that are frequently targeted by ban evasion
communities seeing repeated “throwaway account” join behaviour
Use the Create Link button to generate a new invite link.
Create Link Modal
Realm Select which connected Realm the invite should apply to.
Max Uses (optional) Limit how many successful joins the link can be used for. A value of 0 means unlimited.
Expiration Date (optional) Set a date/time when the link stops working automatically. Leave empty for no expiry.
Operational recommendations:
Use Max Uses for short-term promotions, events, or controlled onboarding.
Use an Expiry Date for public adverts so links naturally rotate over time.
Create separate links for different campaigns (TikTok, Discord, partner servers) so you can disable one source without disrupting others.
Once created, links appear in the Invite Links table.
Invite Links Table
Each entry typically shows:
Realm - which Realm the link targets
Slug / URL - the short link players will open
Uses - current uses vs limit (or unlimited)
Expires In - time until expiry (or “Never”)
Status - toggle to enable/disable the link quickly
Actions - common actions include copying the link and deleting it
Disabled links, expired links, and links that have reached their maximum use count cannot accept further joins.
If a link is being abused, disable it immediately using the Status toggle.
If you want to retire a link permanently, delete it and create a replacement.
Keep older links disabled rather than deleted if you want a record of what was shared and where.
Treat Invite Links as public entry points. Share only what you need, where you need it.
Prefer short expiry for publicly posted links, then rotate regularly.
Enable VPN/Hosting/Tor blocking if you operate a public-code Realm or experience repeated abuse.
Use different links for different platforms so you can identify the source of activity spikes.
Keep at least one “staff-only” link that is never publicly shared for trusted onboarding.

l: The link opens, but the player cannot accept the invite
p: Confirm the link is enabled.
Check whether the link has expired or reached max uses.
If VPN blocking is enabled, ensure the player is not using a VPN/Proxy/Tor.

l: The player accepted, but the Realm does not appear in Minecraft
p: Ask the player to confirm they signed into the correct Microsoft account.
Have them restart Minecraft and refresh their Realms list.
If they accepted on a different Microsoft account, they must repeat the process with the intended account.
Disable the link immediately via the Status toggle.
Create a new link with a tighter Max Uses and an Expiry Date.
Consider enabling VPN/Hosting/Tor blocking if not already enabled.
Change or reset Realm Bot's avatar and nickname for one Discord server.

Bot Server Profile lets you give Realm Bot a custom avatar and nickname in one Discord server. Use it to match your community's branding while keeping the bot's appearance in other servers independent.
This is a Realm Bot Premium feature. It is configured from the server's Overview page and applies to the Discord server as a whole, rather than an individual Minecraft Realm.
Dashboard access to manage the selected Discord server.
Realm Bot present in that server.
Active Premium recognised through the server's linked account.
The bot's Change Nickname permission when changing its nickname.
Select your Discord server in the Realm Bot Dashboard.
Open Overview.
Find Bot Server Profile, below the server information and above Linked User Information.
The card shows the current profile and a preview of pending edits. If the initial profile load fails, use Retry.
Select Change Avatar.
Choose a supported image and review the avatar preview.
Select Save Changes to apply it.
Supported formats are PNG, JPEG/JPG, and WebP, with a maximum file size of 10 MB. GIF uploads are rejected; animated GIF avatars are not supported by this control.
Enter the desired name in Server Nickname, then select Save Changes. The field supports up to 32 characters and includes a character counter.
Clearing the field and saving restores the default bot name. The avatar and nickname can be changed together or independently.
Control
Effect
How to apply it
Reset beside the avatar
Prepare a return to the default avatar
Select Save Changes
Clear Server Nickname
Prepare a return to the default bot name
Reset to Default in the card header
Reset both the avatar and nickname
Select Confirm Reset in the confirmation dialog
The feature changes Realm Bot's member avatar and nickname in the selected Discord server. It does not change:
The bot's application identity or slash-command names.
Its Minecraft account or in-game appearance.
Your own Discord profile or the Discord server's icon.
Its profile in other Discord servers.

Set two values to limit repeated player chat:
Message Threshold - the maximum number of messages allowed before the system triggers

Command
Purpose

Omitting realm applies the action across the account's Realms available through the command. Select one Realm explicitly when you intend to affect only that Realm.

Activation attempts to kick players outside the allowed group. If the command reports that some players could not be checked or removed, the lockdown can still be active. Restore the bot's connection and retry the check; do not assume a partial failure cancelled the restriction.

Turning off Lockdown Configuration pauses enforcement but preserves the saved configuration and active-lockdown state. Turning it back on can therefore resume restrictions.
Changing exemptions or Allow Operators does not automatically check everyone already online again. Run /realm lockdown again for the selected Realm when you need another check.

This is a Realm Bot Premium feature and is currently in Beta. Each Realm has its own configuration under Tools > Realm Stories in the dashboard.
Player posts can include the author's name and avatar, a short text preview, a screenshot when available, a timestamp, and the Realm name. Text previews are limited to approximately 300 characters.

Fix kicks caused by private Xbox title history by setting “Others can see your game and app history” to Everybody.

l: Automod kicked me for “Private Title History”
p: The Private Title History kick means Realm Bot could not use your Xbox game history to check your account, usually to identify your device for a Realm entry rule.
On the Microsoft account you use for Minecraft, set Others can see your game and app history to Everybody, then rejoin the Realm.
Note: If you change this setting back to private later, the same kick may occur again depending on the Realm’s configuration.

l: Fix on Xbox Console (Xbox One / Series X|S)
p: Press the Xbox button to open the guide.
Go to Profile & system -> Settings.
Select Account -> Privacy & online safety -> Xbox privacy.
Select View details & customise.
Open Online status & history.
Set Others can see your game and app history to Everybody.
If you do not see these options or cannot change them, your account may be a child account managed by a family organiser. In that case, a parent or organiser must update the privacy settings.

l: Fix on Web (Nintendo / PlayStation / PC / Mobile users)
p: Sign in to Xbox privacy settings using the Microsoft account you use for Minecraft.
Navigate to Privacy & online safety -> Xbox privacy -> View details & customise.
Open Online status & history.
Set Others can see your game and app history to Everybody.
Allow a little time for the change to apply before rejoining.

You are signed into the correct Microsoft account. Many users have more than one.
Your account is not restricted by family controls.
